newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegalese general to command Brazzaville UN force.
newsitem.headline: Senegalese general to command Brazzaville UN force.

text.p: Senegalese army general Charles Nelson will command a largely African peacekeeping force planned for the embattled Congo Republic capital Brazzaville, Senegalese officials said on Wednesday.
Senegal has accepted a request from the United Nations to head the U.N. force and will itself contribute 500 troops, officials said on Tuesday.
Fighting between supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso has killed hundreds of people in Brazzaville since the conflict began on June 5.
The Security Council authorised U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to sound out mainly African countries about setting up a force of about 1,700 men.

Senegal has participated in several peacekeeping missions, notably in Lebanon, Liberia and Rwanda. Its soldiers are among a U.N. force which has monitored the Kuwait-Iraq border since the end of the Gulf War.
